H: On a finite synthetic artifact corpus, two routes with equal initial task-effect success can have different significant-property survival after deterministic reader-version changes, while preserving harmless transformations and recording open failure as UNKNOWN.

T.metric: synthetic route operation-cost units; not time or real effort

D.pass: All routes satisfy the same initial contract; the auditor detects the planted significant-property losses and render-only degradation, accepts cosmetic-only change, retains failed opens as UNKNOWN, distinguishes post-crossing survival from parse/hash indicators, and detects the frozen case where compact survives better.
D.fail: An open failure is credited as success/failure rather than UNKNOWN; harmless cosmetic change is rejected; parse success or hash identity substitutes for property/render oracle; initial contract differs by route; or controls fail.
D.stop: Source/image/output provenance mismatch or candidate/audit execution failure before a complete interpretable record.

C: Reader outcomes and operation costs are hand-authored. The finite transformations do not model real office-format semantics or software versions. Route labels and relative costs are illustrative.
U: A T0 PASS establishes only scorer sensitivity. It does not establish compatibility across real application builds, long-term preservation, format recommendations, user value, actual repair cost, or product benefit.
